title.narrative: Energy Efficiency in Public Buildings, UNDP

description.narrative:
Green Economic Development fas III har som målsättning att ytterligare främja ökad energieffektivitet i Bosnien och Hercegovina (BiH) och skapa gynnsamma miljöer för investeringar för åtgärder inom energieffektivitet (EE)/ förnybara energikällor (RES). Detta avser främst offentliga byggnader.
Förslaget utgör en logisk fortsättning av projektets andra fas som sedan 2014 implementeras av UNDP och som finansieras av Sida. Den andra fasen kommer att avslutas i februari 2021. Det pågående projektet har hittills uppnått många goda resultat och har lyckats öka energieffektiviteten i BiH. Baserat på förväntningarna av projektets föregående implementeringsfas är det tydligt att projektet bör fortsätta och utökas, även om mycket redan har genomförts. Det finns ett stort behov av förbättringar av offentliga byggnader i BiH, dels för att minska energiförbrukningen och för att reducera utsläppen. I linje med projektmålen består projektet av sju sammanhörande och kompletterande komponenter: - Kapacitetsutveckling (PC1) - utveckla kapaciteten och stärka kunskapen inom miljöministeriet (Ministeriet för utrikes handel och esterna relationer, på engelska förkortat MoFTER), miljöfonderna (Envronmental Funds) och fackfolk inom energiområdet. - Institutionalisering och energihantering (PC2) – institutionalisera, d v s bygga in kunskap och system för, hanteringen av energi, kostnader och utsläppen från offentliga byggnader i BiH. - Juridiska ramverk/finansiella mekanismer (PC3) - utveckla och införa hållbara finansiella mekanismer. - Infrastrukturella åtgärder (PC4) - implementera åtgärder för energieffektivisering i offentliga byggnader. - Allmän kännedom/ marknadsföringskampanjer (PC5) - öka det allmänna medvetandet om energieffektivitet. - RES off-grid-lösningar (PC6) - Förse hushåll som befinner sig utanför nätet med energikällor. - RES/EE i små och medelstora företag (SME) (PC7) - öka RES/EE i SME:s runt om i BiH. Projektet ämnar också bidra till ”grön återhämtning” efter COVID. Detta genom att bidra till teknisk och ekonomisk stimulans för minskade utsläpp av växthusgaser (GHG), förbättrad luftkvalitet, nya jobb, budgetbesparingar/återskapande av resurser för ”gröna” investeringar etc. Halvtids- och avslutande utvärdering av nuvarande GED-projekt (GED II) pågår och kommer att avslutas under början av 2021. Slutsatserna och rekommendationerna från utvärderingen kommer därför, inom ramarna för startperioden, att inkluderas i det nya projektet.

The main goal of Green Economic Development phase III project is to further facilitate scaling up of energy efficiency in BIH and the creation of a favourable environment for investing in Energy Efficiency (EE)/Renewable Energy Sources(RES) measures in BiH, primarily in public sector buildings. The intervention presents logical continuation to the 2nd phase of the Green Economic Project implemented by UNDP and financed by Sweden since 2014, which is coming to its end in February 2021. The ongoing project has achieved many good results and managed in scaling up energy efficiency in BIH. Based on the experience from the previous implementation phases of the Project, though a lot has been done, it is evident that the project should further scale up activities implemented under the GED II, as there is a huge need to improve the public building stock in BiH as to reduce consumption and consequently emissions. In accordance with the goal, the Programme consists of seven interlinked and supplementing project components: - Capacity Building (PC1) – Develop capacity and strengthen skills of MoFTER, Env. Funds staff and energy professionals - Institutionalization of energy management (PC2) – Institutionalization of energy, costs and emission management and monitoring in public sector buildings of BiH - Legislative framework / financial mechanisms (PC3) – Development and adoption of sustainable financial mechanisms - Infrastructure measures (PC4) – Implementation of energy efficiency measures in public buildings - Public awareness / marketing campaign (PC5) – increasing public awareness on energy efficiency - RES off-grid solutions (PC6) – Provide access to energy for off grid households in BiH - RES/EE in SME's (PC7) – Increased EE/RES in SME's in BIH The project also aims to contribute to COVID “green recovery” by providing technical and economic stimulus to GHG emission reduction, air quality improvement, creation of new jobs, budgetary savings/ re-generating resources for investment etc. Mid/end term evaluation of the current GED project is ongoing, and will be finalized in early 2021, therefore findings and recommendations from the evaluation report will be incorporated into new project within the inception phase period.

The primarily goal of Green Economic Development 3rd phase project is to contribute to the creation of a favorable environment for investing in EE and RES measures in BiH. Short-term aim of the GED 3rd phase project is to create interest and motivate end-users to invest into EE/RES by promoting co-financing, develop capacity and skills of Environmental Funds (systematic approach to decision making processes of EE/RES investments) and achieve budget cost savings through implementation of EE/RES projects and reinvest savings into EE/RES or other infrastructure projects. Mid-term aim of the GED 3rd phase project is to generate employment of domestic workforce, increase public awareness and understanding of EE/RES benefits, develop and adopt sustainable financial mechanisms for EE project financing (performance based granting, ESCO Fund window), contribute to BiHs EU accession (EPBD, EED and RES directives) and lower the risk to enter EE investments/provide loans for EE/RES investments in BiH. The project will also contribute to COVID green recovery by providing technical and economic stimulus to GHG emission reduction, air quality improvement, creation of new jobs, budgetary savings/ re-generating resources for investment etc.

title.narrative: Amendment 1 to Agreement to GED III
Amendment 2 to Agreement to GED III

description.narrative: Over four years of implementation (March 2021 - February 2025), in partnership with institutions across all levels of government, the private sector, academia, and civil society, the Green Economic Development Project - Phase III (GED III) has delivered a wide range of results aimed at enhancing Bosnia and Herzegovinas capacity to improve energy efficiency and deploy renewable energy solutions. Building on the achievements of the first two phases, GED III scaled up investments in energy efficiency, promoted renewable energy, created green jobs, and strengthened the institutional framework for sustainable energy management. GED III was implemented through seven interconnected components, which achieved the following results: 1.Strengthened capacities and skills of the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations (MoFTER) and Environmental Funds and energy professionals: The project strengthened the capacities of the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations, both entity's Environmental Funds, and energy professionals through trainings, tools, and institutional support. Through developed strategic documents it enabled government to plan, design, monitor, and implement energy efficiency (EE) and renewable energy (RES) policies more effectively. 2.Established energy monitoring and reporting mechanisms in BiH: GED III established energy monitoring and reporting systems in public institutions, ensuring reliable and consolidated data on energy consumption, costs, and greenhouse gas emissions. This system supports Bosnia and Herzegovina in fulfilling its reporting obligations under the Energy Community Treaty and the UNFCCC. 3.Development of legislation documents in the field of Energy Management, Energy Efficiency, Renewable Energy Sources, E-mobility, and environment which are adopted by the relevant authorities: The project supported the drafting and adoption of by-laws and regulations in the areas of EE, RES, e-mobility, and energy management. These efforts contributed to aligning the national legal framework with EU standards and prepared the ground for the adoption of the National Energy and Climate Plan (NECP). 4.Cost-optimal, green jobs generating and emission reducing EE/RES infrastructure projects implemented in BiH: GED III implemented energy efficiency retrofits in 108 public buildings, including schools (64%), healthcare institutions (13%), and other public facilities such as cultural, administrative, and sports centres (23%), introducing modern heating, insulation, lighting, and solar PV systems. These measures reduced energy use and heating costs by up to 53%, improved indoor comfort, and generated green jobs in construction and energy services. A total of 68 renewable energy systems (RES) were installed and 14 public lighting systems modernized across Bosnia and Herzegovina, creating 2,122 green jobs. Fuel-switch measure was implemented in 534 households.CO emission reduction of 5,315 tones, contributing significantly to the countrys climate goals. The implemented measures resulted in an estimated additional annual CO emission reduction of 5,315 tones, building upon the baseline savings of 13,220 tones, bringing the total cumulative reduction to approximately 18,535 tonnes of CO per year, significantly contributing to Bosnia and Herzegovinas climate goals. Snapshot of the Key results achieved cumulatively under all phases of GED: Energy efficiency improvements in over 300 public buildings, creating measurable and lasting impact. 76 renewable energy systems (RES) installed 14 public lighting systems modernized across BiH. Fuel-switch measures implemented in 534 households, reducing reliance on coal and solid fuels. Annual savings of approx. 7 million BAM Up to 59% overall energy reduction Over 3,500 green jobs created Improved conditions for 670,000 users, including 270,000 women CO emission reductions of approximately 18,535 tones of CO per year. 5.General publics understanding of EE/RES benefits increased: The project increased public understanding of the benefits of EE/RES through outreach campaigns, events, and knowledge-sharing activities. While visibility was strong, the evaluation noted that further targeted advocacy toward policy makers will be needed to accelerate systemic reforms. 6.Access to energy provided for off grid households in BiH: GED III provided renewable energy solutions to 15 off-grid households, significantly improving living standards, particularly for vulnerable families. This demonstrated scalable models of energy access in rural and marginalized communities. 7.Supported implementation of EE/RES projects in SMEs in BiH: 31 SMEs were supported in adopting EE/RES solutions, reducing operational costs, enhancing competitiveness, and preparing for compliance with the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM). These measures fostered innovation and resilience in the private sector. Across all components, GED III mainstreamed gender equality and the principle of Leaving No One Behind. In total, 107,063 women directly benefited, while an estimated total of 244,810 women and girls benefited indirectly through improved public facilities. Vulnerable groups, including children, the elderly, and low-income families, gained improved access to cleaner, healthier, and more affordable energy services. Overall, GED III contributed directly to SDGs 1 (No Poverty), 3 (Good Health and Well-being), 5 (Gender equality), 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure), 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), and 13 (Climate Action). The project also contributed to Outcome 1 of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework 20212025: By 2025, people benefit from resilient, inclusive and sustainable growth ensured by the convergence of economic development, and management of environment and cultural resources, as well as SIDAs objective: Environmentally and climate-resilient sustainable development and sustainable use of natural resources.
